owner_rulings.verbatim: accept the shelter word, accept far seabed reads with the distance printed, 2 km depth radius, CDFW's annual kelp survey.

enc_seabed.name: NOAA ENC Direct (encdirect.noaa.gov) — Seabed_Area layers (S-57 SBDARE)
enc_seabed.caveat: This map service is not intended for navigation purpose.
enc_seabed.license: The service publishes no licence or copyright text (copyrightText is empty on all three bands, read 2026-09-21). NOAA InPort item 39973 (ENC Direct to GIS) states access constraints 'None.' and distribution liability 'None.' — a US government work, openly distributed. Not for navigation; see the caveat.

enc_baseline.note: The probe point, the exposure word and the depth band read R51's own coastline, depth-area, land-area and contour tiles for the chart scale R51 assigned to each entry point.

kelp.publisher: California Department of Fish and Wildlife
kelp.centre: The California Coastal Commission's own published coordinate for the entry point.
kelp.absence_rule: A zero means CDFW's 2016 aerial survey mapped no kelp inside the circle. It is not a statement that no kelp grows there now; in CDFW's own words: "An area where no kelp data are present may represent an area devoid of kelp, or may represent an area where kelp was not detected due to poor photo quality, missing photo coverage, or other issues with data collection and processing."

probe.rule: Tried in this order, the first that passes the test wins. (1) 200 m and (2) 400 m from R51's charted shore point along R51's seaward bearing, where R51 publishes one. (3) Whenever steps 1 and 2 placed nothing — because R51 publishes no seaward bearing, or because both of its points failed the test — the entry point itself. (4) 50, 150, 300 and 600 m past R51's nearest charted water on its own bearing. (5) Otherwise no probe, and the bottom and the depth band are absent with it. The test, for every candidate: inside a charted depth area (DEPARE) AND inside no charted land area (LNDARE), on the chart scale R51 assigned to the entry point. 200 m is this app's convention, not a measurement.

reconciliation.method_trial: derived-metadata-method.md section 0, measured 2026-09-22 over all 1,575 entry points: 1,312 by the seaward bearing, 98 past the nearest charted water, 17 with the pin in charted water, 40 absent, 108 with no chart. This build's own counts are in coverage.probe.
reconciliation.rule_change: R59-D fix 2 (ruling 3): step 3 is tried whenever steps 1 and 2 placed nothing. The first R59-D build tried the pin only where R51 publishes no seaward bearing and counted 1,312 / 104 / 8 / 43 (seaward / past water / pin / absent). Nine entry points move under the rule above, each to the pin: six that were placed past the nearest water (ccc-129, ccc-242, ccc-288, ccc-992, ccc-1271, ccc-1282) and three that were absent (ccc-197, ccc-550, ccc-1098). Every one of the nine has an R51 seaward bearing whose 200 m and 400 m points both failed the test, and a pin inside a charted depth area and outside every charted land area.
reconciliation.ccc-121: Pedrazzini Boat Ramp (ccc-121) is absent although R51's nearest_water reads inside: true. R51's inside flag tests the charted DEPTH areas only. This derivation's test also refuses a point inside a charted LAND area, and on the coastal chart scale R51 assigned to this entry point the pin lies inside a charted depth area AND inside a charted land area, so it is refused. R51 publishes no seaward bearing here, and none of the points 50, 150, 300 and 600 m past the nearest charted water on its bearing passes the same test.

bottom.rule: Of every seabed-area feature (point, line, area) NOAA charts on the chart scale R51 assigned, the one nearest the probe point; an area containing the probe scores 0 m. NATSUR is copied verbatim and never mapped; a blank NATSUR is carried as null and read as 'charted, nature of surface not recorded'. NOAA's SORDAT (source date), SORIND (source indication) and DSNM (chart cell) for the feature ride beside every answer, null where the feature carries none.

exposure.spot: R51's charted shore point for the entry point
exposure.seaward: R51's seaward bearing ('chart'); where R51 has none, the bearing from the charted shore point to the probe point ('probe')
exposure.measured: A component is measured only where its test could be run. A bay or pocket test that finds no charted coastline about its arm length away on one side, or on both, records measured: false with missing_side (left, right or both), pts: null and offset_m: null — an unmeasured test is never a 0. The headland test walks every charted coastline within 2 km; where no charted coastline lies within 2 km it is not measured either (reason: no charted coastline within 2 km). score is the sum over the MEASURED components only, and score_of the most those components could score (bay 2, pocket 1, headland 1; 4 when all three were measured). The word is given ONLY when all three components were measured; otherwise word is null and the row reads 'Exposure not fully measured', with the score printed as 'score N of M measured' and each unmeasured component named with the arm that found no coastline.
exposure.arms: Left and right are as seen standing on the shore looking out to sea along the seaward bearing: the right arm lies toward the seaward bearing + 90 degrees, the left arm toward - 90 degrees.
exposure.conventions: Stated by this app where section 3 is silent, and standing as the definition of the word: smoothing = the 50 m resample plus the 210–390 m arms (no moving average), headland turn > 45°, arm tolerance 20% ('about' an arm length is within 20% of it). Charted coastline pieces whose ends meet within 1 m are walked as one line; the sea side of any chord is the side the spot's own seaward bearing points to. No swell direction is assumed anywhere.
exposure.record: every exposure record carries the word (null unless all three components were measured), the score, score_of and its three components: bay, pocket and headland, each with measured and its points (null when not measured)
exposure.ends: each arm end as [metres, bearing] from the spot, the right arm (looking out to sea) first
exposure.sectors: each headland as [bearing, metres] from the spot

depth_band.rule: Measured from the probe point. The shallow line is the charted contour nearest 3 m among those from 1.5 to 6.0 m, the deep line the one nearest 20 m among those from 14.0 to 26.0 m; the band is reported only when both exist, each with its own charted value and its distance. United States charts publish no 3.0 m and no 20.0 m contour.

kelp.rule: spear_kelp.json's own row for the entry point, copied: CDFW's annual aerial canopy survey, measured by R60 Lane K1 inside 500 m of the Coastal Commission's coordinate. Not derived a second way.

method.rounding: whole metres and whole degrees; coordinates six decimals

copy.exposure_caveat: This word describes the shape of NOAA's charted coastline around the entry point, not today's swell. Monastery Beach reads sheltered on this geometry.
copy.bottom_caveat: The nature of the seabed NOAA charts nearest a point in the water off this entry point, at the distance printed. It is a fact about a chart, not about the bottom under a diver.
copy.depth_band_caveat: Charted depths are metres below chart datum, which for United States waters is mean lower low water. They are not the depth at the moment you are reading this. The band is the charted contour band, not a typical dive depth.
copy.probe_note: The point in the water is 200 m (or 400 m) off NOAA's charted shore along its seaward direction, or the entry point itself where it stands in charted water, or just past the nearest charted water; 200 m is this app's own convention, not a measurement.
copy.natsur_not_recorded: charted, nature of surface not recorded
copy.service_caveat: This map service is not intended for navigation purpose.

absent_reasons.no_chart: NOAA's electronic charts show no coastline and no charted water within 2 km of this entry point, so nothing here was measured in the water. Nothing is estimated in its place.
absent_reasons.no_probe: No point in charted water could be placed off this entry point: 200 and 400 m out along the charted shore's seaward direction where the chart gives one, the entry point itself, and 50 to 600 m past the nearest charted water — every point tried was on charted land or outside every charted depth area. Nothing is estimated in its place.
absent_reasons.no_seabed_feature_within_2km: NOAA charts no seabed-area feature within 2 km of the point in the water off this entry point, so the chart says nothing here about what the bottom is made of.
absent_reasons.no_shore: No charted coastline within 2 km of this entry point, so there is no coastline shape to describe.
absent_reasons.no_seaward_direction: The chart does not settle which side of the coastline here is the water, and no point in charted water was placed off this entry point, so the coastline's shape cannot be read against the sea.
absent_reasons.no_shallow_line: Within 2 km of the point in the water off this entry point, NOAA charts no depth contour between 1.5 and 6.0 m, so there is no shallow line to report.
absent_reasons.no_deep_line: Within 2 km of the point in the water off this entry point, NOAA charts no depth contour between 14.0 and 26.0 m, so there is no deep line to report.
absent_reasons.no_lines: Within 2 km of the point in the water off this entry point, NOAA charts no depth contour between 1.5 and 6.0 m and none between 14.0 and 26.0 m.
absent_reasons.not_in_kelp_file: The kelp survey file this dataset carries has no row for this entry point.
